Clause quoted from the current rights holder (WHO, doc WHO/UCN/MSD/MHE/2024.1): "Some rights reserved. This work is available under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 IGO licence (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO). Under the terms of this licence, you may copy, redistribute and adapt the work for non-commercial purposes." That is a stated non-commercial use restriction from the originator, and under the 2026-09-05 HEXACO ruling (irw#1945) any stated use restriction from the wording's rights holder blocks, whatever the deposit licence. The deposit here IS permissive -- PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0294357 is CC BY 4.0 and its S7 file carries the response data -- but originator-governs (DSES/ECR-R line), so the deposit does not clear it. Register note also warns specifically: do NOT clear a WHO-5 table on the Psychiatric Research Unit's permissive homepage; copyright was assigned to WHO in 2024. Instrument identity confirmed rather than assumed (Step 3b): live table is 5 items W1-W5, resp 0-5, 122 person-waves over 61 respondents at 2 timepoints -- the canonical WHO-5 shape; biblio Description reads "WHO-5 Well-Being Index (5 items, 0-5 scale) at baseline and 2-week follow-up"; data/wakui_2023_who5.py melts WHO5_ITEMS=["W1".."W5"] from the S7 workbook. The block does bite: item codes W1-W5 are opaque source column headers, so no WHO-5 wording is already exposed in the response table (contrast irw#2101/#2123). Administered language was Japanese (tags.csv: jpn), which does not change the verdict -- a translation is a derivative of the restricted instrument. No __items.csv written; no mapping verification row written, since a blocked table has no live item text to carry a verification outcome (SKILL.md Step 5b). RETRY TEST: NO -- determinate. An unchanged retry right now returns the same answer; nothing was inaccessible (the paper, its S7 data file and the register were all read). To flip it, WHO would have to relicense the WHO-5 without the NonCommercial term, or Ben would have to overrule the register's block verdict.

Gate-clean pass carrying two caveats. (1) option_text is blank for all 27 rows: the paper gives only the anchors of a '7-point' distress/sympathy scale ('not at all' to 'very much') while both S1 and the live table store eight codes 0-7, so no anchor could be assigned to a code without guessing; wtc_amount is an open 0-100 donation amount with no labelled options. (2) Mixed-language administration: 208 of 371 respondents read an unpublished Chinese version (including 'one hundred Yuan (about 15 $)' in place of 'one hundred dollars'); language='Chinese; English', base fields hold the paper's English, no _translated columns, per the szameitat_2015_* precedent. (3) instructions blank -- the paper describes the leukemia vignette but does not reproduce the stimulus text.
